facts.statement: Peteinosaurus had an estimated wingspan of about 60 cm, making it one of the smallest and earliest known pterosaurs, though some estimates suggest it may have reached 1 meter.
facts.quote: With an estimated wingspan of about 60 cm, it was among the smallest and earliest known pterosaurs, although some estimates suggest that its wingspan may have reached 1 m.

facts.statement: Peteinosaurus had an elongated fifth toe that lacked a claw.
facts.quote: Its fifth toe was elongated and lacked a claw.

facts.statement: The genus Peteinosaurus was described by the German paleontologist Rupert Wild in 1978.
facts.quote: The genus has been described by the German paleontologist Rupert Wild in 1978.

facts.statement: The genus name Peteinosaurus is derived from the Greek words peteinos, meaning "winged", and sauros, meaning "lizard".
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from Greek peteinos, "winged" and sauros, "lizard", the latter being used to indicate any saurian.

facts.statement: Peteinosaurus likely inhabited the continent of Pangea during the middle Norian stage of the Triassic (approximately 221 to 210 million years ago) along the shores of the ancient Tethys Sea, where the foothills of the Alps in northern Italy are located today.
facts.quote: Probablemente habitó en el continente de Pangea en el período Triásico a mediados del Noriense (hace unos 221-210 millones de años). Vivió en las orillas del antiguo mar de Tetis, donde hoy se encuentran las estribaciones de los Alpes, en el norte de Italia.

facts.statement: Peteinosaurus's wings were proportionally smaller than those of later pterosaurs, as the wing length was only twice the length of its hind limb.
facts.quote: Sus alas eran también proporcionalmente menores que las de los pterosaurios tardíos, ya que la longitud del ala era solo el doble de larga que la de su extremidad posterior.

facts.statement: All other known pterosaurs had wingspans that were at least three times the length of their hind limbs.
facts.quote: Todos los otros pterosaurios conocidos tenían envergaduras que eran al menos el triple de la longitud de sus miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: Peteinosaurus had teeth with a single cusp that lacked the specialized heterodonty present in the other Italian Triassic pterosaur genus, Eudimorphodon.
facts.quote: También tenía dientes con una sola cúspide que carecían de la especializada heterodoncia presente en otro género de pterosaurio italiano del Triásico, Eudimorphodon.

facts.statement: These factors suggest Peteinosaurus belonged to the most basal known group of pterosaurs, the Dimorphodontidae, to which it was assigned in 1988 by Robert L. Carroll.
facts.quote: Todos estos factores juntos hacen suponer que Peteinosaurus pertenecía al grupo más basal conocido de pterosaurios: los Dimorphodontidae, al cual asignado en 1988 por Robert L. Carroll.

facts.statement: However, cladistic analyses have not demonstrated a close connection between Peteinosaurus and the genus Dimorphodon.
facts.quote: Sin embargo los análisis cladísticos no han demostrado una conexión cercana entre ambas formas.

facts.statement: Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia affirmed the possible basal position of Peteinosaurus and suggested that Preondactylus, considered by David Unwin to be the most basal pterosaur, might be a subjective junior synonym of Peteinosaurus.
facts.quote: Aun así la posible posición basal de Peteinosaurus ha sido afirmada por Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia quien sugirió que Preondactylus, que de acuerdo con David Unwin es el pterosaurio más basal, podría ser un sinónimo más moderno subjetivo de Peteinosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2010 cladistic analysis by Brian Andres and colleagues placed Peteinosaurus in the group Lonchognatha, which includes Eudimorphodon and Austriadactylus as more basal.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico de 2010 realizado por Brian Andres y colegas sitúa a Peteinosaurus en el grupo Lonchognatha el cual incluye a Eudimorphodon y a Austriadactylus como más basales.

facts.statement: Mark Witton, however, considers Peteinosaurus to be a true dimorphodontid.
facts.quote: Mark Witton, sin embargo, considera a Peteinosaurus como un verdadero dimorfodóntido.
